criterion: P1b-AC3 second half (both incidents COMPLETE in one transaction)
chain: decision -> incident -> Smart Record window -> sealed clip -> published clip with manifest -> CLIP delivery entry -> PUT api/v1/relay/clips/{id} -> backend export -> upstream accept -> receipt transaction completing every contributor
rig_caveat: The facility hub is simulated: a mock answering the three calls the backend makes (capabilities, clip PUT, state PUT), an enrolment row written directly into edge_site, one camera bound to a backend_camera_id, and API_BACKEND_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=1 which the product documents as a local-fixture switch. Everything downstream of that - the worker delivery queue, the export client, the backend export route, the media verification and the receipt transaction - is unmodified product code.
verdict: The chain completes: one clip, 38 contributor incidents COMPLETE, 38 distinct artifact rows on that clip. Read as a code-path proof, not as a production acceptance.
claim_strength: SIMULATED INTEGRATION EVIDENCE, not production evidence. It establishes that the code path from a published clip to completed contributor incidents works; it does not establish that it works against the facility hub. A review called the earlier PASS wording overclaimed and it is withdrawn here.
not_established: behaviour against the real facility hub, including its auth and error shapes
atomicity under a forced mid-transaction failure - no rollback case was exercised
that the alerts were produced at a meaningful threshold: this run used the 0.0-threshold proof bundle so the episodes themselves carry no clinical meaning
